title: Vasquez’s close: determinate true assent yes; fearless or infallible faith-certainty no
source_text: XXIV. Denique his consentit Vasquez, sic claudens cap. 9. Disputationis illius 200. saepius jam citatae: Concludamus igitur, posse quidem justum certum esse de sua gratia, certitudine sumpta pro determinato & vero assensu, non tamen certitudine sumpta pro assensu sine formidine ulla, neque pro certitudine cui non possit subesse falsum, & ita de certitudine loquimur in hac controversia.
pass_a_gloss: Finally Vasquez agrees with these, thus closing chapter 9 of that Disputation 200 so often already cited: Let us conclude therefore that the just person can indeed be certain of his grace with certainty taken for determinate and true assent, yet not with certainty taken for assent without any fear, nor for certainty to which falsehood cannot be subject; and so we speak of certainty in this controversy.
pass_b_english: Vasquez sums up: the just may have determinate true assent about grace.
He denies both fearless assent and infallible faith-certainty in this debate’s sense of ‘certainty.’
